label: Affine Shape Spaces
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 135 to 146 and builds the affine shape space of k landmarks in dimension m. We quotient configurations by translation and the full general linear group, the natural symmetry whenever a planar scene is viewed through varying affine cameras across many frames.

label: Why Affine Invariance
notes: An affine camera maps a flat scene by an invertible linear map plus a shift, so the same object yields sheared and scaled landmark sets across views. Affine shape discards exactly that nuisance, retaining only the structure shared by every affine image of the configuration in question.

label: Configurations and Centering
notes: We start from k labelled landmarks in real m space, stacked as a matrix. Subtracting the centroid removes translation and lands us in the centered subspace, the first quotient step before the general linear group acts on the remaining centered coordinate columns of the landmark matrix.

label: The Affine Group Action
notes: Translation plus the general linear group acts on landmark matrices. After centering, an invertible linear map acts on the right of the centered coordinate matrix, mixing its columns. Two configurations share an affine shape precisely when one centered matrix equals the other times such an invertible matrix.

label: Affine Shape as a Subspace
notes: Right multiplication by invertible matrices never changes the column span of the centered configuration. The orbit is therefore captured exactly by that span, an m dimensional subspace of the centered coordinate space, provided the landmarks are in general position so that the rank stays full and well defined.

label: The Grassmann Identification
notes: Collecting all such spans identifies the affine shape space with a Grassmann manifold of m dimensional subspaces inside a k minus one dimensional space. This compact manifold inherits a clean geometry, turning affine shape analysis into honest statistics on a Grassmannian rather than on raw coordinates.

label: Projection-Matrix Embedding
notes: Each subspace is represented uniquely by the orthogonal projection onto it, the matrix P equal to U times U transpose for any orthonormal basis U. This equivariant embedding into symmetric matrices is the bridge that makes extrinsic mean computation a linear-algebra exercise on averaged projection matrices.

label: Extrinsic Mean
notes: Embed each affine shape as its projection matrix, average those matrices in the ambient Euclidean space, then project the average back. The extrinsic mean is the subspace spanned by the dominant eigenvectors of the mean projection, the directions carrying the most shared affine structure across the sample.

label: Existence and Uniqueness
notes: The extrinsic mean exists and is unique when the average projection matrix has a clear eigenvalue gap separating its top m eigenvalues from the rest. A spectral gap guarantees a well defined dominant eigenspace, so the projection back to the Grassmannian becomes single valued and stable.

label: CLT and Two-Sample Tests
notes: Under the embedding the sample extrinsic mean obeys a central limit theorem in the tangent space at the population mean. Its asymptotic covariance powers confidence regions and two sample tests that compare affine mean shapes between groups without assuming any parametric model for the landmarks.

label: Application: Scene Matching
notes: Because affine shape is invariant to affine camera distortion, projection-matrix features match a planar scene across viewpoints and recognize landmark patterns like digit shapes. The chapter notebook builds exactly these affine features, discarding the similarity information that ordinary Procrustes analysis would have kept instead.

label: Summary and Outlook
notes: Center, take the column span, embed by projection, and average: affine shape analysis becomes Grassmannian statistics with extrinsic means, central limit theorems, and tests. The same recipe extends to projective shape in the next chapter, where the symmetry group grows once more beyond the affine case.
